name: Chicken Tinga
summary: Shredded chicken in a smoky tomato and onion sauce, served with warm corn tortillas and rice.
instructions: Put the chicken and bay leaves in a pot, cover with water, add 1 tsp salt, and simmer 30 minutes. Lift out the chicken, keep 250 mL of the broth, and shred the meat off the bones. Discard skin and bones.
Cook the rice: 200 g rice with 400 mL water, simmered covered for 15 minutes, then rested 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, smoked paprika, chili, oregano, and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and the reserved broth. Simmer 8 minutes until thick.
Stir in the shredded chicken and simmer 5 minutes. Serve with warm tortillas and rice, two tortillas per person.

glutenFree.notes: Corn tortillas are naturally gluten-free, but a few brands add wheat flour. Check the label.

budgetNotes: Substitution: smoked paprika and chili powder replace chipotle peppers in adobo, which are hard to find in Ottawa chain stores. The taste changes: chipotles add a deep, smoky heat with a vinegary tang from the adobo sauce. Smoked paprika gives the smoke but much less heat and none of the tang, so this version is milder and sweeter. If you find a can at a Latin grocer, use 1–2 chopped peppers plus a spoon of the sauce instead of the paprika.
Leftover tinga makes good tostadas: bake corn tortillas until crisp and pile it on.
The poaching broth is free chicken stock. Freeze the rest for soup.
